newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-CSKA PLEDGE IMPROVEMENT UNDER NEW COACH SADYRIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CSKA PLEDGE IMPROVEMENT UNDER NEW COACH SADYRIN.

text.p: Russian premier league club CSKA Moscow, confirming the appointment of former national team coach Pavel Sadyrin, pledged on Monday to improve dramatically under his leadership.

"New coach Sadyrin is well known at CSKA, under whom the team won the (Soviet) league title in 1991," said Alexander Baranovsky, head of the CSKA sports club which is 60 percent owned by the defence ministry. "We expect the team will drastically improve its performance under him."
Baranovsky, speaking at a news conference, dismissed attempts by Sadyrin's predecessor Alexander Tarkhanov to hang on to his job.

When CSKA first announced Sadyrin's appointment on New Year's Day, Tarkhanov, who guided the side to fifth in the 1996 Russian championship, said he had not been told of his sacking and had no plans to resign.
But Baranovsky said: "The team failed to produce the results we expected, so the sacking of Tarkhanov is routine."

Club officials said they would not let Tarkhanov's protests destroy a team which was briefly disbanded once before -- by late Soviet dictator Josef Stalin after the national side, dominated by CSKA players, was beaten 5-0 by Yugoslavia in the 1952 Olympic Games in Helsinki.
"We shall not let anybody tear apart our team like in 1952," said CSKA official Valentin Nikolayev, who played in the side humiliated in Helsinki.
CSKA notched up seven Soviet league titles and won the Soviet cup five times but have not tasted success since the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991 and the Russian league began.
Sadyrin, 54, is starting his second spell at CSKA after parting company with Zenit St Petersburg at the end of last season after they finished 10th in the league.
He was sacked as Russia's national coach after a stormy two years which ended in failure at the 1994 World Cup finals after several players boycotted the team.
